'''Jan Sickmann Hesthaven''' (born 10 December 1965) is a Danish mathematician,<ref name="EPFL biography">{{cite web|title=Jan S. Hesthaven - Biography|url=https://people.epfl.ch/jan.hesthaven/?lang=en#biography|access-date=8 May 2020|archive-date=19 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200519052018/https://people.epfl.ch/jan.hesthaven?lang=en#biography|url-status=live}}</ref> currently president of the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]].<ref name="KIT">{{Cite web|title=President Jan S. Hesthaven|url=https://www.kit.edu/eb/president.php|access-date=25 October 2024|archive-date=14 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241014231647/https://www.kit.edu/eb/president.php|url-status=live}}</ref> He was previously Vice President for Academic Affairs (starting in 2021)<ref>{{Cite web|title=New EPFL Vice-Presidencies approved|date=25 September 2020|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/new-epfl-vice-presidencies-approved|access-date=9 August 2021|archive-date=20 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920025552/https://actu.epfl.ch/news/new-epfl-vice-presidencies-approved/|url-status=live}}</ref> at [[EPFL]] ([[École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne]]) and held the Chair of Computational Mathematics and Simulation Science (MCSS).<ref name="EPFL page">{{cite web|title=Jan S. Hesthaven - EPFL personal page |url=https://people.epfl.ch/jan.hesthaven/?lang=en|access-date=8 May 2020}}</ref> He is particularly known for contributions to the development, analysis and application of high-order accurate computational methods for time-dependent partial differential equations.<ref name=SIAMFellow/> He has also contributed substantially to the development of reduced order models and the application of neural networks and machine learning techniques to problems in science and engineering.

== Career ==
Prof. Hesthaven<ref name="EPFL biography"/> obtained a Master of Science degree in computational physics from the [[Technical University of Denmark]] (DTU) in 1991. In 1995, he received a Ph.D.  in Numerical Analysis from the Institute of Mathematical Modelling ([[Technical University of Denmark|DTU]]) and in 2009 he was awarded the degree of Dr.Techn. from [[Technical University of Denmark|DTU]] for substantial and lasting contributions that has helped to move his research area forward and penetrated into applications.

After graduation, he was appointed in 1995 as Visiting Assistant Professor at [[Brown University]], then in 1999 as assistant professor and in 2003 he was promoted associate professor of [[applied mathematics]] with tenure at [[Brown University]] where in July 2005 he was promoted to professor of applied mathematics.

In 2006, he founded the [https://ccv.brown.edu/ Center for Computation and Visualization (CCV)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809024633/https://ccv.brown.edu/ |date=9 August 2020 }} at [[Brown University]] and was its director until 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biography|url=https://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/jansh/page22/page22.html|website=www.cfm.brown.edu|access-date=2020-05-08|archive-date=3 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703174758/http://www.cfm.brown.edu/people/jansh/page22/page22.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He served from Aug 2010 to June 2013 as founding deputy director of the Institute of Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics [[ICERM]], an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Mathematical Sciences Research Institute.

In 2013, he joined  [[EPFL]] ([[École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne]]) where he was appointed full professor of computational mathematics and simulation science,<ref>{{cite web|last=Evangelista|first=Sandy|date=2012-07-12|title=Eight professors appointed at EPFL|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/eight-professors-appointed-at-epfl-14/|language=en}}</ref> and shortly later, in February 2014, he founded the new unit of Scientific IT and Application Support (SCITAS)<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rezzonico|first1=Vittoria|last2=Robyr|first2=Julien|date=2014-03-16|title=Développer l'utilisation des superordinateurs de l'EPFL|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/developper-l-utilisation-des-superordinateurs-de-l/|language=fr|access-date=8 May 2020|archive-date=20 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230820043810/https://actu.epfl.ch/news/developper-l-utilisation-des-superordinateurs-de-l/|url-status=live}}</ref>

From 2016 to 2021 he served as Editor in Chief of [[SIAM]] Journal of Scientific Computing.

In February 2017, he became dean of the School of Basic Sciences (SB).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Papageorgiou|first=Nik|date=2017-01-24|title=Jan S. Hesthaven appointed Dean of EPFL's School of Basic Sciences|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/jan-s-hesthaven-appointed-dean-of-epfl-s-school--4/|language=en}}</ref> In September 2020, he was appointed as Vice President for Academic Affairs at EPFL for a term starting in 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Board appoints new members of the Executive Boards of ETH Zurich and EPFL {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/board-appoints-new-members-of-the-executive-boards-of-eth-zurich-and-epfl|access-date=2020-09-25|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=20 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420154907/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/board-appoints-new-members-of-the-executive-boards-of-eth-zurich-and-epfl|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In January 2024, he was elected as the future president of the German [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)]] by the supervisory board.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Landgraf |first=Monika |date=2024-01-23 |title=Supervisory Board Elects Jan S. Hesthaven President of KIT |url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2024_005_supervisory-board-elects-jan-s-hesthaven-president-of-kit.php |access-date=2024-01-24 |publisher=[[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] |language=en-gb |archive-date=24 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124092326/https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2024_005_supervisory-board-elects-jan-s-hesthaven-president-of-kit.php |url-status=live }}</ref> The election was confirmed by the Senate on 19 February 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Landgraf |first=Monika |date=2024-02-19 |title=KIT Senate Confirms Election of Jan S. Hesthaven |url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2024_33584.php |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=[[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] |archive-date=19 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219161554/https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2024_33584.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has assumed the presidency as of the 1st of October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lehné |first=Margarete |date=2024-04-10 |title=Jan S. Hesthaven Will Assume Presidency of KIT in October |url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/202404-hesthaven-will-assume-presidency-of-kit-in-october.php |access-date=2024-04-12 |website=[[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] |archive-date=10 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240410225141/https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/202404-hesthaven-will-assume-presidency-of-kit-in-october.php |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Brown University gave him their  Philip J. Bray Award for Teaching Excellence in 2004.<ref name=BrayAward>{{cite web |title=Brown University Faculty Teaching Excellence Awards |url=https://www.brown.edu/about/administration/dean-of-faculty/faculty-teaching-award |access-date=21 April 2020 |archive-date=7 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107165331/https://www.brown.edu/about/administration/dean-of-faculty/index.php?q=faculty-teaching-award |url-status=live }}</ref>
He was elected as a [[SIAM]] Fellow in 2014.<ref name=SIAMFellow/> He was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to computational methods for PDEs, high-order accurate methods, and the reduced order method".<ref name=fams>{{cite web |title=AMS Fellow |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#h |access-date=25 January 2025 |archive-date=18 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211118112432/https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#h |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2022 he was inducted as member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]].<ref name=RDASL>{{cite web|title=Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters |url=https://royalacademy.dk/author/janhesthaven/}}</ref> In 2023, he was elected as a member of [[Academia Europaea]]<ref name=AE>{{cite web|title=Member of Academia Europaea |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Hesthaven_Jan}}</ref> and the [[European Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=EurASc>{{cite web |title=Member of European Academy of Sciences |date=13 April 2022 |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/jan-s-hesthaven/member/ |access-date=25 January 2025 |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125111128/https://www.eurasc.eu/members/jan-s-hesthaven/member/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2024, the [[Technical University of Denmark]] awarded him an honorary doctorate in recognition of his scientific contributions <ref name=DTUhc>{{cite web |title=Hononary Doctorate DTU |url=https://www.dtu.dk/om-dtu/profil/begivenheder-og-priser/aeresdoktorer |access-date=25 January 2025 |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125104123/https://www.dtu.dk/om-dtu/profil/begivenheder-og-priser/aeresdoktorer |url-status=live }}</ref>
